name: @platform/api
description: Standalone Express API. Owns the database, the cron scheduler, and payment webhooks.
//test: --test-concurrency=1 is deliberate. Node's runner defaults to one process per test file, and each opens its own Prisma pool against the database over Railway's TCP proxy. The proxy tolerates far fewer concurrent connections than that, so the parallel default produced failures that were not about the code — 'Server has closed the connection', 'Unable to start a transaction in the given time', and 500s from requests downstream of a dead link — which cost time across several steps before the cause was found. Serial is slower on a remote database and honest. If the suite ever runs against a local Postgres, this can be revisited.
//dependencies: prisma is a runtime dependency, NOT a devDependency. Do not move it back. Railway does not install devDependencies in production, and the pre-deploy container runs `prisma migrate deploy` from the application image — Railway's own docs require that a pre-deploy command 'has the dependencies it needs to run installed in the application image'. With prisma in devDependencies the pre-deploy step fails with empty logs, because the binary is simply absent. @prisma/client is the runtime library; prisma is the CLI that runs migrations and generate.
